# HOLD

Holds entities waiting in a queue until a named signal fires, a condition becomes true (a buffer has room, a machine is idle), or for good.

Infinite mode never releases: the entity stays held in the store for the rest of the run. That is the documented semantics, not a leak.

Family: control. Python builder: `m.hold(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use HOLD to keep entities waiting until something outside the flow happens: a shift starts, a gate opens, a buffer has room, a machine is idle. In `Signal` mode, a [SIGNAL](signal.md) block releases them. In `Condition` mode, the entity waits until its own tests are true. `Infinite` mode parks entities for good.

## Behaviour and rules

All waiting entities sit in the block's store, so the `store_summary` frame reports how many wait and for how long. In `Signal` mode, the entity waits for the next broadcast of that signal name. A signal that fires before the entity arrives is missed. The signal is not remembered.

A signal releases every entity waiting on that name at that instant. They then leave one by one in the same instant. In `Condition` mode, all conditions must be true. An entity whose conditions are already true passes without waiting.

The block re-checks the conditions whenever something they read changes, such as a variable, a queue length, a resource state, a store or a level threshold. If a condition reads the clock, a time series or a random draw, nothing announces a change. The block then also re-checks every `scan_interval`.

In `Infinite` mode, the entity never leaves. It stays in the work in progress until the run ends. This is intended and not a leak.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `'Signal'` |  |  |  | "Signal": wait for a named signal. "Condition": wait until every condition is true, re-checked whenever something it reads changes. "Infinite": never release. |
| `signal_name` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Name of the signal to wait for, when mode is "Signal". |
| `conditions` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Boolean expressions that must all be true to release, when mode is "Condition". |
| `scan_interval` | float | `1.0` |  | time | `scan_interval_unit` | Fallback re-check interval, when mode is "Condition": used only when a condition reads something no event announces (TNOW, TS(), RAND(), a level between events). Variables, NQ/NR/MR/IDLE, NS and threshold writes wake it at once. |
| `scan_interval_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `scan_interval`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |

## Statistics

Every run fills `system` and `entity_summary` (see the [KPI reference](../kpis.md)). The example below also fills:

| Frame | Columns |
|---|---|
| [`store_summary`](../kpis.md#store_summary) | `Run`, `Store`, `Capacity`, `Average Size`, `Max Size`, `Mode Size`, `Mode Size %`, `P95 Size`, `P99 Size`, `Std Size`, `Avg Time in Store`, `Mode Time in Store`, `Mode Time in Store %`, `P95 Time in Store`, `P99 Time in Store`, `Std Time in Store`, `Util % (time-weighted)` |
| `material_flow_summary` | `Run`, `From`, `To`, `Entities` |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=100)
m.create("Parts", distribution=nb.Constant(value=1), max_arrivals=10) >> m.hold(signal_name="Open") >> m.dispose()
m.create("Gate", distribution=nb.Constant(value=1), max_arrivals=1, start_time=30) >> m.signal(signal_name="Open") >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(int(results.kpi("system/Total Entities Completed")), "entities completed: the 10 held parts and the one that sent the signal")
print(round(results.kpi("store/hold_1_hold/Average Size"), 2), "parts held on average")
```

```text
11 entities completed: the 10 held parts and the one that sent the signal
8.5 parts held on average
```
